name: AdvancedEncryption.WE.Codes.card_le_of_sparse_preimages
title: Sparse preimages are expensive: if every target has a preimage of support at most rho, then |T| <= ((N+1)|F|)^rho
statement: Let F be a finite alphabet with a zero, f a map from F^N to a finite set T, and suppose every t in T has a preimage x with at most rho nonzero coordinates. Then |T| <= ((N+1)|F|)^rho. For a linear map onto F^n this gives rho >= n log|F| / log((N+1)|F|): a Hamming-metric gadget matrix with sparse preimages of every target has heavy columns, so one level of BGG+-type evaluation on LPN samples multiplies the noise weight by at least n / log((N+1)|F|) (note pq-we-non-lattice-algebras).
